text: The barber looked startled. <break time="0.8s" /> But Bernice calmly took the chair. <break time="0.8s" /> And minutes later. <break time="0.8s" /> Her long, beautiful hair. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay on the floor around her. <break time="0.8s" /> When she looked into the mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> She saw not a daring beauty. <break time="0.8s" /> But a plain, pale girl. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose bare neck. <break time="0.8s" /> Made her look strangely helpless. <break time="0.8s" /> Warrens face grew cold at once. <break time="0.8s" /> And on the way home. <break time="0.8s" /> He spoke only politely to her. <break time="0.8s" /> As though the spell had been broken forever. <break time="0.8s" /> Her aunt was horrified as well. <break time="0.8s" /> And looking at Marjories satisfied smile. <break time="0.8s" /> Bernice finally understood. <break time="0.8s" /> That her cousin had planned the whole humiliation. <break time="0.8s" /> That night. <break time="0.8s" /> After packing her bag for a late train. <break time="0.8s" /> Bernice crept into Marjories room. <break time="0.8s" /> Where her cousin lay sleeping. <break time="0.8s" /> With two long golden braids. <break time="0.8s" /> With a pair of shears in her hand. <break time="0.8s" /> She carefully cut off both braids. <break time="0.8s" /> And Marjorie. <break time="0.8s" /> Sleeping soundly. <break time="0.8s" /> Did not wake up at all. <break time="0.8s" /> Then she slipped out of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Carrying her bag and the braids. <break time="0.8s" /> And on her way to the station. <break time="0.8s" /> She passed Warrens house. <break time="0.8s" /> Laughing wildly. <break time="0.8s" /> She flung the golden braids onto his porch. <break time="0.8s" /> And ran on toward the station. <break time="0.8s" /> Leaving the town and her cousin behind.
